messages:
elaine: quick heads up — after yesterday's kernel-scheduler tweak i'm seeing a ~10-15% p99 bump on streaming ingress paths. not across all customers but heavy-token workloads. attaching a short profiler dump below.

elaine: perf summary:
```
host_ingress_streaming p50 12ms p95 48ms p99 210ms (was 185ms)
kv-cache hitratio 0.82 -> 0.78
syscall writev count +18% on hot paths
```

mike: thanks. do we have a flame/sample that shows where the extra time is going? kernel or user parsing?

elaine: initial stack samples point to more time in preparse/tokenize + small writev syscalls (more fragmentation). not confident about kernel selection effects.

sanjay: posted a 5s perf script snippet from a canary:
```
# top stacks (count)
user:preparse::tokenize  42
user:runtime::dispatch   18
kernel:writev           27
user:kvcache::lookup    15
```
seems like more writev+syscalls per request vs before.

anna: could be batching-window interplay with the new kernel hinting. the scheduler now prioritizes smaller windows for latency SLOs which might reduce coalescing upstream.

raul: ran a quick strace microbench vs previous build:
```
old: total writev calls per request = 6
new: total writev calls per request = 9
avg chunk size shrank 28%
```
that aligns with the syscall delta.

mike: ok plausible chain: kernel scheduler -> shorter kernel-run slices -> runtime emits smaller streaming chunks -> more writev/syscalls -> p99 tail. also kvcache hit ratio drop might be because of different batching ordering.

elaine: can we triage two angles in parallel: 1) kernel-selection rollback A/B on canary traffic, 2) change preparse coalescing to force 1 writev per logical frame and see effect. who can run 1 and 2?

mike: i can run the kernel-selection A/B on canary cluster. will toggle flag --kernel-preference=balanced vs latency and collect p50/p99 + syscall counts. starting now.

sanjay: i'll instrument preparse coalescer. quick patch to bump coalesce window from 2ms -> 6ms and add metric token_coalesce_groups. will push to a smoke canary.

anna: fyi ci-bot triggered a deploy pipeline for the coalesce patch:
ci-bot: build/7890 started for eng-runtime/coalesce-wip (PR #4821) :github:

ci-bot: deploy to canary-cluster-3 succeeded (3245012360) :white_check_mark:

raul: mike — any preliminary numbers from the kernel flag flip?

mike: flipped flag at 3245012368 for 10% of canary traffic, collecting 5m windows. early: p99 back down ~6% for that cohort, writev counts down ~12%. still collecting.

elaine: great. if both mitigations move the needle we can do a layered fix: keep kernel hint improvement but add upstream coalescing and tweak batching heuristic to preserve kvcache ordering.

sanjay: agree. hypothesis: kernel hinting was fine for compute but interacting poorly with our streaming chunk heuristics. will open issue and add perf test case that asserts max writev per request. filing now — #RI-1567.

mike: i'll keep A/B running and share dashboards. tagging @anna for batching heuristics changes next. :thumbsup:

anna: on it. will try a conservative batching reorder (preserve kvcache affinity) and run offline microbench before rolling.

elaine: thanks all. clear action items in the issue. i'll add the flamegraphs and the strace samples to the thread.

elaine: TL;DR: p99 tail from streaming due to more fragmented writes after kernel scheduler change -> two-prong mitigation (kernel flag A/B + upstream chunk coalesce) looks promising. follow-up in RI-1567. :mag:
